summary: Round 4 — sharing feature verified end-to-end. All 46 pytest backend cases pass (14 new round-4 share tests + 32 regression from rounds 1-3). Frontend E2E: public /share/:token page renders without auth/token in localStorage, showing author+fallback-initial avatar, 'sent you a postcard' eyebrow, view count, chapter title, body excerpt, 'Made with warmth on A–Z Haven' footer, and 'Make your own →' CTA. Bad token shows shared-error block. /postcards: share-0..share-2 buttons present; ShareLinkModal opens → loading → share-url row (data-testid share-url + share-copy) with 4 social buttons having correct hrefs (twitter.com/intent/tweet, facebook.com/sharer, wa.me, mailto:) all containing the share URL. Copy button clicked — clipboard blocked in headless as expected, toast displays 'Couldn't copy. Long-press...'. detail-share button present in postcard detail modal. PostcardModal has postcard-share-link testid wired. Cleanup: models.py has single last_daily_greeting_at declaration; voice.py content-type if-block removed (tests assert this).

issues: shared-image has no max-height cap — when an oversized/stretched thumb is passed, the card becomes extremely tall. Consider adding max-h-[70vh] or object-cover to shared-image. Non-blocking; real postcards from canvas are well-proportioned.

Detail modal can scroll very long when thumbs are full-resolution pet photos; detail-share button ends up below the fold (functional but ergonomics: sticky footer with actions would be nicer). Non-blocking; pre-existing from round 3.

action_items: Optional polish: add `max-h-[70vh] object-contain` to shared-image in SharedCard.jsx so oversized thumbs don't stretch the card vertically.
Optional polish: make the postcard detail-modal footer sticky so detail-share is always visible without scrolling.
critical_code_review_comments: backend/routes/share.py: GET /share/{short_id} returns the doc BEFORE incrementing views ($inc runs after find). End users see 0 on the very first view. Acceptable but slightly counter-intuitive — if you want the response to reflect the current view, swap to find_one_and_update with returnDocument='after' in a single atomic step.
backend/routes/share.py: 850KB thumb cap is generous for a data URL (that's ~637KB binary base64-decoded). Fine — just flagging it's tighter than many social-card norms; no action.
frontend/src/pages/SharedCard.jsx: uses raw axios (no JWT auth) — correct for a public page. Good isolation. One nit: no viewport meta enforcement, but index.html likely already has it.

frontend/src/components/ShareLinkModal.jsx: POST /share/postcard fires on every modal open for the same postcard — no caching by chapter_index. If the user toggles the modal repeatedly, N rows accumulate and count toward the 100-cap. Consider a small per-chapter_index session cache or a 'reuse-if-exists-in-last-day' lookup.

success_rate.frontend: 100% on all probed selectors: shared-page, shared-card, shared-error, shared-title/body/views/cta, share-0..2, share-modal, share-url, share-copy, share-twitter/facebook/whatsapp/email, share-close, detail-share, postcard-share-link (verified in source)

context_for_next_testing_agent: Round 4 tests at /app/backend/tests/test_round4_share.py. Run all rounds: `cd /app/backend/tests && python -m pytest -v --junitxml=/app/test_reports/pytest/results.xml`. To E2E the /share/:token page, any POST /api/share/postcard response's short_id is usable on the frontend without auth — that's the feature. ShareLinkModal POSTs on open, so in playwright seed localStorage az_token + az-haven-save-v3 with at least one postcard in `postcards` array, navigate to /postcards, and click share-{index}. Clipboard API is blocked in headless Chromium; tests should verify UI state transitions (button text) rather than system-clipboard contents.
rca of the issue: No bugs. One test-script self-correction: initially asserted `doc.views >= 1` on first public GET, but backend does find_one → return → update_one (async fire-and-forget), so the pre-increment value (0) is returned on the very first hit. Updated assertion to check type + added a separate increments-on-subsequent-read test.
